stories.author: @ahorseofficial
stories.text: I've never been into playing video games so much, but I loved to watch my brother play them when I was young. Back then my mother was still alive, my family was all so close. It was warm, carefree. Since then many things had happened and my brother and I grew apart. A decade plus some years later, I found this song again. I have no musical talent, but I was determined to learn this song at least partially on the piano. When I came home from school one day my mother had coincidentally purchased a really old piano and placed it in the living room. The next morning as my brother was still sleeping, I focused and played this song to the best of my lackluster ability. My brother wakes up and barrels down the hallway trying to figure out the song that I was playing was and why he remembers it so well. After a few guesses he says "Kingdom Hearts?" I like to think ever since that moment we have been slowly reforming our bond. We are nothing alike and agree on almost nothing as adults, but at least that one moment will stay with me forever.

stories.author: @internetphenomenon734
stories.text:
I'm 33 years old. I lived in a big house with a few acres of woods behind it. I have 4 siblings - one is my older brother by two years, another my younger by two years. The three of us, and occasionally my FOURTH brother, would play together in the woods when we were kids. I loved those woods. We would pretend all the standard fare for 00's kids - Pokemon, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, even some Digimon. We had wild imaginations, and our adventures always had to do with fighting evil creatures, or catching Pokemon, if that was the flavor of the day. I was homeschooled, so I didn't have to deal with public school and its pressures.

Kingdom Hearts was a favorite of mine, even though I hardly ever played. I watched older bro play it and let my mind create the adventure. It was fun watching him play it, we had pretty much grown out of pretending. When I heard Dearly Beloved for the first time, I was at the same stage as Sora. I was on an idyllic island with only a few of my closest friends, where nothing much happened. But I could feel it - I was ready to go. The outside world was beckoning, with all its adventures, and I had to answer.

Of course I left the island, and of course it was painful. Growing always is. But I will never forget those memories - excitement and safety, the feeling that there in those woods, with my friends, I had everything I needed. This song reminds me of that safety, and of the bittersweet voyage towards Purpose that all of us must take.

stories.author: @Tweekitus
stories.text:
Fuck me... I bought this game without knowing exactly what I was getting into. 22 years later, I can't help but think back to the time when I first dipped my toes into KH1. It was so captivating, and I remember crying like a baby at the ending when Kairi and Sora were separated.

This series will genuinely go down in history. It can be argued that it is genuine emotional porn, but at least we got characters who felt real. Sora knows he's not the smartest, but he trusts in his friends and realizes that having people to back him up makes him stronger. Riku lost his way, but he realized how wrong he was and fought tooth and fucking nail to make it right, eventually accepting that he could use the parts of him that he disliked to help do good.

Yes, you have to suspend your disbelief a bit and accept the fact that the storytelling tends to lean toward "if it sounds/feels good, it works," but I will never in my life regret the story that I got to experience. And KH1 began it all with a little boy who just wanted to see what the greater world was really like.

For those like me who experienced this game on or near it's release date... You guys remember? Remember how it seemed to drag your mind into a state where you were convinced you may have been dreaming during your first time going through the dive to the heart and doing the intro sequence? Then you get into the initial quests on the island, you do the race, you collect supplies, you go swimming all over the beachfront on both sides, convinced there is some kind of secret to discover? Remember how you got so comfortable that it approached boring?

I (in my very young mind) was actually convinced that we'd go out on that raft and run into the Disney characters we were promised on some small-medium islands that were located around the ocean. Tbh I anticipated a fairly mild adventure. Then things started to get weird, ansem in the cave was the first sign that things werent gonna go how I expected, then waking up to the storm, hearing this theme, meeting Darkside... It was crazy. 

Then to my complete shock, we hit traverse town. To this day that town is among my top 5 list of fictional places I'd like to live in if I one day woke up sucked into a fictional world. Man the design of that place.. such wonderful nostalgic memories.

stories.text: What i feel when i hear this song is Longing. I long for the days when i was young, for when i visited my older cousin playing together and like Sora and Riku, the days before the family drama, before the school trauma, the days where i was blisfully unawear of my crippling loneliness, the days where i could hang out with my best friend without realizing that he began to distance himself from me. I still have dreams about it all, my Classmates, my best friend, my cousin, but i know they don’t care, none of them do. They’ve never cared enough to know how i was doing, to ask me if i wanted to hang out with them, to try and contact me again even after so long. Sometimes i think about that scene, the one where Sora flies through the darkness, and reaching the light of his heart, Kairi, Riku, Donald, and Goofy all being that light, the ones who keep him going, and always bring him back from the darkness, and i just can’t help but feel jelous of it. It’s stupid, he’s a fictional character, but he still has so much, his heart is always with his friends, and theirs are all with him aswell, but i’ve never had that, i’ve never had someone fill that void i’ve had in my heart since i was 13. Back then, i was young and naive, unawear of it even being there, but now i very much do. And maybe one day i’ll finally find it, that light i keep reaching out to, maybe a friend, maybe a brother, maybe a Partner or even a Lover, and maybe when i do, these dreams will finally end. But i don’t have my hopes up, because i’m already a lost cause. I hate this feeling.

I have so many memories of this song. The first was my first time hearing the song. I already knew that I was going to Hollow Bastion and that it was late game, but I had no idea about this track. I immediately though "Oh shit, we're approaching end game! This song is epic!" Before I learned about Youtube, I went through this route repeatedly just to hear this song.

stories.author: @deegeayy
stories.text: End of the World’s theme and level design was just so mesmerizing to me as a kid. The theme is practically a reprise of the first song you hear in the game, but fuller. The first view you have is an event horizon of purples and blues amongst a seemingly endless sea of nothing. Then, as you press on, you venture through shards of worlds you thought you saved. Seeing the Hundred Acre Wood here of all places was shocking to 10 year old me. Then, at the *end* of the end, you find yourself back on a fragment of Destiny Islands… the place where it all began. I hadn’t played any other games that went this deep into level design when I was younger. So this easily stands out as one of the best places in gaming. Even if this place wasn’t as impactful as The World That Never Was, it’s still a stellar final world

stories.author: @internetphenomenon734
stories.text:
I'm 33 years old. I lived in a big house with a few acres of woods behind it. I have 4 siblings - one is my older brother by two years, another my younger by two years. The three of us, and occasionally my FOURTH brother, would play together in the woods when we were kids. I loved those woods. We would pretend all the standard fare for 00's kids - Pokemon, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars, even some Digimon. We had wild imaginations, and our adventures always had to do with fighting evil creatures, or catching Pokemon, if that was the flavor of the day. I was homeschooled, so I didn't have to deal with public school and its pressures.

Kingdom Hearts was a favorite of mine, even though I hardly ever played. I watched older bro play it and let my mind create the adventure. It was fun watching him play it, we had pretty much grown out of pretending. When I heard Dearly Beloved for the first time, I was at the same stage as Sora. I was on an idyllic island with only a few of my closest friends, where nothing much happened. But I could feel it - I was ready to go. The outside world was beckoning, with all its adventures, and I had to answer.

Of course I left the island, and of course it was painful. Growing always is. But I will never forget those memories - excitement and safety, the feeling that there in those woods, with my friends, I had everything I needed. This song reminds me of that safety, and of the bittersweet voyage towards Purpose that all of us must take.

stories.author: @Tweekitus
stories.text:
Fuck me... I bought this game without knowing exactly what I was getting into. 22 years later, I can't help but think back to the time when I first dipped my toes into KH1. It was so captivating, and I remember crying like a baby at the ending when Kairi and Sora were separated.

This series will genuinely go down in history. It can be argued that it is genuine emotional porn, but at least we got characters who felt real. Sora knows he's not the smartest, but he trusts in his friends and realizes that having people to back him up makes him stronger. Riku lost his way, but he realized how wrong he was and fought tooth and fucking nail to make it right, eventually accepting that he could use the parts of him that he disliked to help do good.

Yes, you have to suspend your disbelief a bit and accept the fact that the storytelling tends to lean toward "if it sounds/feels good, it works," but I will never in my life regret the story that I got to experience. And KH1 began it all with a little boy who just wanted to see what the greater world was really like.

stories.author: @Corpse.Candy.666
stories.text: This song gives me two feelings. Calmness, and sadness. I don't know why. I hear it, and suddenly I'm drifted into a state of uncertainty and sorrow. But I know I'm not alone. I have my partner, and my friends. Yet, I still feel lonely. I don't know what to do, but this music emphasizes it. I like it, but it hurts. It hurts. I feel lonely, but at the same time, I feel a weight being lifted off of my shoulders. Like this music carries away my stress and worries, even if I still feel sad. Either way, I want to forever remember this song, and never lose it. Because when that day comes, and I'm left alone at my own stand... I want to play this song, and remind myself of who I really am. Just before I do anything. At least then I can have a bit of happiness before I go.

stories.author: @somethingofnote9241
stories.text: Its already been four years since I first experienced this gem of a series, and yet somehow, this song is just as nostalgic to me as it was when I first heard it. No matter the occasion, my mood, how long I listen to it, etc., it never fails to remind me of times long gone, never failing to make me weep. There's something about this melody that resonates so strongly with the human soul that it feels like its always been a part of it. This song is your family, your parent's cooking, your closest friends, your pets, your childhood home, your first kiss, your high school graduation, that one memory that is so unbelievably inconsequential but you never fail to forget, and countless more experiences put into sound all at once. Like the waves of the ocean, memories wash over you until you are enveloped by the sea of your soul. A true dive to the heart.

Right now, I'm looking at the medals in my hands and thinking, 'How did I end up like this? What did I do wrong? Do I still have time to change?' Tears are threatening to leave from my eyes, but I just feel empty inside. I don't recognize the current me, and the past seems so distant. I don't know if I will have the strength to fulfill my dreams... I don't know if I can ever free myself from these chains, and even if I do, the future frightens me the most... I'm so lost. 

All I can do is silently dream, dream about the skies, dream about a world where people are more caring and loving. Dream about a world where people can understand each other feelings regardless of their origins and languages. That's why I dream -- because it's limitless and I'm not bound by the chains of reality.
